subject: Coordination: term cycle calendar and deprecation playbook for ACME MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@acme-retail.com>, Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Term cycle calendar alignment — ACME MSA + Order Form

Hi Hannah / Mark,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As we start to stitch the MSA and Order Form together I wanted to align on three operational items that our legal and finance teams flag frequently:

- Auto-renew mechanics (how many renewal terms, notice window to opt-out, and automatic prorations)
- Termination for convenience and operational transition timing (what constitutes a reasonable wind-down window)
- A shared calendar for notice triggers so both sides can automate reminders

High-level asks from our side: we generally propose a 12-month initial term, one automatic 12-month renewal unless notice delivered 60 days prior, and a termination for convenience with 90 days of service continuity to allow for data export and KV cache drain. That 90-day request is mostly operational — it lets us run graceful handoffs without impacting production.

I've attached a redline of the MSA highlighting the suggested language and a draft Order Form with the renewal knobs set to our standard defaults. Please review and let me know the items you want to discuss with procurement/legal on your side.

Next steps: if you agree in principle, can we lock a short call with your procurement and legal this week? Karthik, looping you to coordinate.

Best,
Jordan
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.docx, OrderForm_ACME_v2_redline.pdf

From: Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@acme-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Pat Collins <pat.collins@dlapiper.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term cycle calendar alignment — ACME MSA + Order Form

Jordan — thanks for the note and the redlines. A few quick points from our side after an initial pass:

1) Renewal notice window: our standard for similar SaaS providers is 30 to 60 days. We prefer 60 days maximum; 90 is long for us operationally.
2) Auto-renew cap: we are comfortable with one automatic 12-month renewal, but not perpetual auto-renew. After the automatic renewal we would like the option to renegotiate rather than auto-extend again.
3) Termination for convenience: we understand the need for an operational window, but 90 days is heavy on our side — can we do 60 days? We need to ensure continuity with our downstream vendors.

I copied Pat from our counsel to help with the legal framing. We're happy to get on a call Friday afternoon. Hannah, are you available?

Thanks,
Mark
Director, Strategic Sourcing
ACME Retail

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@acme-retail.com>, Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@acme-retail.com>, Pat Collins <pat.collins@dlapiper.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term cycle calendar alignment — ACME MSA + Order Form

Team — sharing legal perspective and two proposed options inline. See attached MSA redline for context (Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.docx).

Option A (Redwood preferred, operationally safer):
- Initial term: 12 months.
- Auto-renew: one automatic 12-month renewal.
- Renewal notice: customer must provide written notice to opt out at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term.
- Termination for convenience by either party with 90 days written notice; provider commits to assist with data export and a transition runbook.

Rationale: 90 days gives our ops team room to drain KV caches and reassign capacity without causing dropped sessions; it also allows time to export embeddings and user data in a manner that preserves integrity.

Option B (compromise to close deal quickly):
- Initial term: 12 months.
- Auto-renew: one automatic 12-month renewal.
- Renewal notice: 60-day opt-out (same as A).
- Termination for convenience: 60 days written notice plus a limited SLA for handover assistance capped at 4 weeks of active runbook support (beyond that we will invoice at committed hourly rates).

We propose Option B if ACME needs to keep the termination window to 60 days. This gives them a predictable handover while protecting Redwood operationally (we reserve the right to invoice for extended migration support).

Open items for negotiation: whether auto-renew is capped at one renewal (we'd prefer language that prevents perpetual renewals without express written agreement) and the effective cutover timing in the Order Form's billing section.

Attaching the redline. Karthik/ Jordan, can you surface any commercial pushback if ACME insists on 60 days with no additional handover warranty?

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.docx

From: Pat Collins <pat.collins@dlapiper.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@acme-retail.com>, Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term cycle calendar alignment — ACME MSA + Order Form

Stephanie / Jordan — quick comments from ACME's counsel. We appreciate Redwood's operational constraints. A few practical suggestions that usually bridge the gap: 

- 60-day termination notice is commercially reasonable if coupled with a 30-day prioritized migration window where Redwood provides dedicated migration hours (e.g., up to 80 hours of senior engineer support) at no additional cost. That keeps the visible transition smooth.
- For auto-renew, consent to cap at one automatic renewal is acceptable; add a clause that requires renewal amendments to be mutually agreed for further auto-renewals.
- Include an early-exit data escrow clause: in the event of termination for convenience, Redwood deposits critical metadata (not full model weights) into an escrow for 120 days to ensure ACME can rehydrate sessions with minimal impact.

If Redwood is willing to commit to the migration hours and the escrow window, ACME will accept a 60-day termination window. Happy to draft the precise language and exchange a short form amendment for signatures.

Best,
Pat Collins
Partner, DLA Piper (external counsel for ACME)

Note: suggested language attached in their redline PDF.

Attachment referenced: OrderForm_ACME_v2_redline.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@acme-retail.com>, Mark Rivera <mark.rivera@acme-retail.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term cycle calendar alignment — ACME MSA + Order Form

Thanks, everyone — good progress. Short summary and next steps so we have a clean action list:

1) Commercial compromise: ACME will accept a 60-day termination-for-convenience window if Redwood agrees to provide 30 days of prioritized migration support (up to 80 hours of senior engineering time) at no additional charge.
2) Auto-renew: Redwood agrees to cap auto-renew at one automatic 12-month renewal; further renewals require mutual written agreement.
3) Data escrow: Redwood will deposit critical session metadata into escrow for 120 days post-termination; Stephanie to confirm scope (metadata vs. any PII or model weights).

Action items:
- Stephanie: prepare a short amendment that implements the 60-day termination with the 30-day migration commitment and the escrow language, and attach to the redline. Target: 24 hours.
- Karthik: confirm commercial routing with finance for the migration support commitment (will we treat as included as a one-time onboarding credit or amortize over term?). Target: EOD Monday.
- Hannah/Mark: confirm ACME procurement sign-off on the amendment text once received.

Laura, looping you for awareness and quick sign-off on the migration support commitment if needed.

Would anyone prefer a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize language or should we just exchange the amendment doc? I'll prioritize a call if ACME wants it.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none (see prior redlines)
